forces.title: Always-on inspiration through social media fuels travel ideas.
forces.description: Travel inspiration has become an ambient condition, delivered continuously through social feeds, film, and AI, often before explicit intent is formed. This "always-on" inspiration creates numerous entry points for destinations and experiences to enter a traveler's consideration set. Social media, in particular, inspires 60% of trip ideas and influences 70% of travelers to consider new destinations, reshaping the initial discovery phase for OTAs and tour operators.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Fragmented research journey imposes "restart tax" on travelers.
forces.description: The travel research process involves an increasing number of tools and touchpoints (search, reviews, OTAs, supplier sites, AI), leading to fragmentation. Each handoff between platforms strips away context, forcing travelers to re-enter preferences, retype dates, and re-evaluate options. This "restart tax" causes frustration and increases decision fatigue, as travelers must reconstruct their decision map repeatedly. For OTAs and tour operators, this friction makes it harder to retain traveler attention and guide them towards a booking.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI increasingly influences travel discovery, but trust remains a barrier.
forces.description: AI tools are rapidly becoming a significant source of inspiration, with a quarter of initial inspiration sessions involving AI, offering speed from vague ideas to detailed itineraries. However, traveler confidence in AI lags its technological advancement, with questions regarding authenticity, reliability, and pricing. While AI can narrow options, human-validated trust from friends, reviews, or credible creators remains crucial for conversion. This creates a challenge and opportunity for OTAs and platforms to integrate trusted elements into AI-driven discovery.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Travelers seek curated shortlists, not overwhelming options, to ease decision-making.
forces.description: Consumers are overwhelmed by the sheer volume of choices and information available during travel research, leading to anxiety about making wrong decisions. Instead of vast searchable catalogs, 63% of travelers prefer a curated set of ten recommended options. They desire credible shortlists with clear reasoning, rather than merely more filters. This shifts the competitive advantage to players who can effectively narrow options and provide validated recommendations, presenting an opportunity for OTAs and tour operators to improve their curation and recommendation engines.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Holistic wellness definitions drive broader consumer spending across categories.
forces.description: Consumers are expanding their definition of fitness beyond mere exercise to encompass overall wellbeing, including mental health, longevity, and stress management. This holistic view leads them to invest across a wider range of wellness categories such as gym memberships, fitness experiences, and wellness services. This structural shift creates tailwinds for Travel, Tourism & Leisure, particularly for segments like wellness retreats, fitness centers, and activity-based leisure facilities, as consumers allocate more discretionary spending towards these broader wellness pursuits.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: Key life stages accelerate wellness spending, creating acquisition opportunities.
forces.description: Consumer wellness spending significantly accelerates during pivotal life stages, such as youth sports participation, weight-loss journeys, and setting new fitness goals. These "accelerant moments" are characterized by heightened motivation and a greater willingness to invest in new products, experiences, and brands. For leisure facilities and wellness providers, these moments represent powerful opportunities to acquire new consumers, encourage trade-up, and build long-term loyalty by tailoring offerings to specific, evolving needs.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: AI-driven discovery reshaping how consumers find wellness products and services.
forces.description: Consumer discovery of wellness solutions is increasingly shifting towards AI-driven recommendations. Instead of searching for individual products, consumers use AI to ask broader, holistic questions like "What gear do I need for my first marathon?" AI's ability to combine products, advice, and training plans into a single experience makes it influential, with over 50% of consumers using AI across wellness occasions. This necessitates that wellness and leisure providers optimize for generative engine optimization to ensure visibility in AI-generated recommendations.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: Improved air access boosts inbound travel and tourism recovery.
forces.description: Enhanced air access has significantly supported Ireland's inbound tourism recovery, with trips to the country increasing by 18% year-on-year in the first five months of 2026. European trips rose by 24% and North American trips by 15%, with holiday travel being the strongest segment, up 30%. This trend provides a strong tailwind for OTAs and tour operators focused on the Irish market, indicating higher demand for packages, experiences, and associated services from international visitors.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Easing State-contracted accommodation gradually increases tourism supply.
forces.description: The phased withdrawal of State-contracted accommodation, expected by March 2027, is gradually returning registered tourism bed stock to the commercial market. Nationally, the share of tourism beds under State contract has fallen from 13.0% in summer 2023 to 3.7% in May 2026. This measured increase in available accommodation capacity provides a supply-side tailwind for the Travel, Tourism & Leisure sector, potentially improving availability for OTAs and tour operators, and supporting destination capacity in previously constrained regions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical risks directly reduce discretionary travel demand.
forces.description: Geopolitical uncertainty and conflicts are directly influencing travel decisions, evident in reduced airline spending. Higher long-haul costs and security concerns are weighing on inbound sentiment, corporate travel confidence, airfares, and demand for higher-value, long-haul travel. While softer outbound air travel may boost domestic staycations, a sustained deterioration in geopolitical conditions poses a significant risk to the overall Travel, Tourism & Leisure sector, impacting bookings for OTAs, tour operators, and leisure facilities reliant on stable international demand.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Shorter booking windows and last-minute travel alter demand patterns.
forces.description: Operator feedback indicates a trend towards shorter booking windows and a rise in last-minute bookings across the hospitality sector. This shift in consumer behavior presents both challenges and opportunities for OTAs and tour operators. While it requires more agile revenue management and inventory allocation, it also creates possibilities for dynamic pricing strategies and real-time promotions. Adapting to this quicker decision-making cycle is crucial for optimizing capacity utilization and maximizing revenue in a volatile market.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Direct booking strategies intensify competition for online travel agencies.
forces.description: Hospitality operators are increasingly prioritizing direct booking strategies and experience-led packages to enhance profitability and customer relationships. This acceleration of direct-to-consumer efforts intensifies competitive pressure on Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) and tour operators, who traditionally served as intermediaries. OTAs must adapt by offering differentiated value, enhanced loyalty programs, or unique package deals to retain market share against suppliers aggressively pursuing their own distribution channels and focusing on curated experiences.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: New travel customer journey demands continuous engagement and trust building.
viewpoints.description: The traditional linear travel planning path has evolved into a complex, iterative "orbit" with over 65 touchpoints. Travelers are continuously exposed to inspiration but lack commitment, making sustained attention crucial. Success requires earning credibility and smoothing friction across platforms, as travelers frequently switch ideas or restart research. Operators need to create continuity and confidence from inspiration to post-booking, focusing on building trust to secure bookings in this fragmented environment.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: AI speeds travel planning, yet struggles to build essential traveler trust.
viewpoints.description: AI tools can rapidly generate detailed itineraries, offering speed from vague ideas to specific plans. However, traveler confidence in AI is not advancing at the same rate. Despite polished AI outputs, users still seek human-like trust and validation through reviews, friends, or direct supplier sites to confirm perceived quality, authenticity, and best pricing. This highlights a gap where AI can narrow options but human-touch credibility ultimately drives booking decisions, presenting a challenge for AI-driven platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Booking confirmation is a waypoint, not the end, demanding post-booking relationships.
viewpoints.description: Booking a trip no longer signifies the end of the customer journey, but rather a "waypoint." Continuous inspiration, flexible policies, and ongoing price monitoring mean travelers frequently reconsider or change bookings even after confirmation. This creates significant opportunities for travel players to foster active post-booking relationships, maintain engagement, and extend the traveler's experience. Businesses that recognize this shift can leverage it to build loyalty and reduce cancellations by providing ongoing value and reassurance.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Global wellness economy presents substantial growth opportunities for brands to capitalize.
viewpoints.description: The global wellness economy is experiencing robust growth, outpacing many discretionary spending categories. This expansion is driven by consumers broadening their definition of fitness to encompass overall wellbeing and investing across a wider range of wellness categories. Brands, including those in activewear, have a strong foundation to capture this growth by engaging consumers during pivotal life stages, extending into adjacent wellness areas through tailored products and experiences, and adapting to AI-driven discovery channels.
viewpoints.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

viewpoints.title: Dublin's H2 2026 hospitality outlook cautiously positive, facing geopolitical risks.
viewpoints.description: The H2 2026 outlook for Dublin's hospitality market is cautiously positive, with an expected RevPAR growth of 1.1% over 2025, supported by summer demand, air capacity, and events. However, geopolitical risks are a direct demand variable, as higher long-haul costs and security concerns are already influencing travel decisions. While softer outbound air travel may support domestic staycations, sustained deterioration in global conditions could weigh on inbound sentiment, corporate travel confidence, and long-haul demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Consumers are increasingly viewing fitness through the lens of overall wellbeing, leading to investments across a broader set of wellness categories including fitness experiences and wellness services.
Wellness spending accelerates or decelerates at key life moments (e.g., youth sports participation, weight-loss journeys, setting new fitness goals) creating acquisition and retention opportunities.

new_opportunities.description: Brands can capture more consumer wellness spending by tailoring core offerings, expanding content, and forging partnerships in areas like gym memberships, fitness experiences, and wellness services as consumer definitions of wellness broaden.

Brands need to compete for visibility within AI-generated recommendations as consumers increasingly use AI for wellness product discovery, especially during high-intent life stages for more holistic solutions.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted annual growth rate for the global wellness economy, outpacing many discretionary categories.
market_sizing.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

demand_drivers.description: As wellness ecosystems mature in countries like France and Germany, a growing share of future wellness spending is expected to shift towards adjacent categories beyond activewear, such as gym memberships, fitness experiences, and wellness services.

new_opportunities.description: Activewear brands have an opportunity to capture a larger share of the wellness wallet in France and Germany by expanding into adjacent categories like fitness experiences and wellness services.

market_sizing.methodology: Activewear's share of consumers' overall wellness spending in France and Germany compared to the US market. The report suggests other markets may head towards the US model.
market_sizing.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?
